recipes.projection: Blended projection = weighted mean of Sleeper app x1, FantasyPros x1, CBS Sports x1, ESPN fantasy x1, DraftKings points converted from each source's own stat lines. Weights renormalise over the sources that cover each player; coverage is the covering weight as a share of the total enabled weight. Coverage under 50% keeps the number from the sources that do cover the player and is flagged "thin"; it is never pulled toward a typical score for the salary. No coverage leaves the projection blank, flagged "no projection", unless the injury report lists the player as out, on IR, doubtful or suspended, in which case the projection is 0.
recipes.ownership: Own% is the average, by source weight, of the numbers Weekly findings file, Footballguys percent rostered and RotoWire projected roster % published for the DraftKings main slate; numbers for any other site or slate are never used. Stokastic DK cheat sheet is downloaded, stored and shown in its own column, but never averaged into Own% (weight 0). A number Adam types into the Own% cell replaces the published one for that player. A player with no published number is left blank: the app never estimates ownership, so game popularity exists only where a real number does.
recipes.scoring: DraftKings scoring from stat lines; 100/300-yard bonuses paid as 3 x probability from a lognormal (cv rush 0.55, rec 0.55, pass 0.30); DST points-allowed from a normal around the opponent's implied total (SD 9.5, shutout rate unvalidated)

injury.comment: Smith-Njigba reeled in seven of 10 targets for 51 yards during Sunday's 17-3 win against the Cardinals.
injury.longComment: Smith-Njigba was working with backup QB Drew Lock for the third time this season, as the latter was filling in for Sam Darnold (quadriceps/rib). The result was a season low in receiving yards, which was only the second time this season in which Smith-Njigba failed to reach the century mark. Despite the subpar outing for him, he surpassed 1,000 yards on the campaign for a third straight season, with eight games still to go. Darnold may also be sidelined next Sunday at Las Vegas, which again could impact Smith-Njigba's chances to produce as he has most weeks in 2026.

injury.comment: Walker (groin) has been ruled out for Sunday's game against the Falcons, Jordan Schultz of Fox Sports reports.
injury.longComment: Walker was a late addition to the Chiefs' practice report Friday as a DNP due to what was described as "groin tightness." He was initially tagged as questionable for Sunday's contest, but the injury is severe enough for the fifth-year running back to miss his first game of the regular season. Rookie fifth-rounder Emmett Johnson is projected to lead Kansas City's backfield against Atlanta in Walker's absence, and with Jaydn Ott (hamstring) listed as questionable, the Chiefs could elevate Nate Carter from the practice squad to the active roster. Walker's next opportunity to play is Week 11 against the Cardinals on Sunday, Nov. 22.

injury.comment: The Rams placed Nacua (knee) on injured reserve Thursday.
injury.longComment: With this transaction officially in the books, Nacua will be required to miss at least the next four games due to the PCL and MCL sprains and turf-toe injury that he sustained near the end of this past Sunday's win at Washington. During the initial stage of Nacua's absence, the Rams will lean on Konata Mumpfield, Tutu Atwell, CJ Daniels and Xavier Smith at wide receiver until Davante Adams (hamstring) is ready to return from injured reserve.

injury.comment: Lamb brought in 10 of 16 targets for 195 yards and a touchdown in the Cowboys' 27-23 win over the Colts on Sunday. He also lost a fumble.
injury.longComment: Lamb easily led the Cowboys across the board in receptions, receiving yards and targets in a game that Dallas was operating without George Pickens (hamstring). Lamb's yardage total was a new season high, and he rounded out his stellar day with his seventh touchdown catch of the campaign on a 44-yard grab just before halftime. Even his turnover had a bright side to it from a fantasy perspective, as Lamb gained 44 yards on an impressive downfield catch and picked up extra yardage after the Colts initially failed to touch him down before fumbling at the end of that sequence. Lamb has four straight double-digit target games and is just 96 yards away from his sixth consecutive 1,000-yard season heading into a Week 10 home showdown against the 49ers next Sunday.

injury.comment: Robinson carried the ball 19 times for 100 yards and a touchdown and caught six of seven targets for 47 yards in Sunday's 34-17 loss to the Bengals.
injury.longComment: Backup Khalil Herbert handled just three touches, as Robinson dominated the workload in the Atlanta backfield with his usual No. 2, Brian Robinson (hamstring), on the shelf. It was the first time since Week 4 that Bijan had reached the century mark in rushing yards, and also the first time since that game against the Saints he got into the end zone. Robinson will look to build upon this effort in Week 10 against Kansas City.

injury.comment: The Colts informed Taylor that he won't be traded before Tuesday's deadline, Tom Pelissero of Netflix reports.
injury.longComment: In order to move Taylor, Indianapolis was reportedly seeking a blockbuster trade package on par with what Carolina received in exchange for Christian McCaffrey back in 2022, but Pelissero relays that inquiring teams weren't willing to meet that price tag. As a result, Taylor -- who is under contract through 2028 -- will stick around in Indianapolis through the remainder of the campaign, though it's possible that the Colts entertain trade offers for the 27-year-old running back again during the offseason.

injury.comment: Bowers caught seven of eight targets for 111 yards and a touchdown in Sunday's 38-17 loss to the 49ers. He also rushed once for two yards and lost a fumble.
injury.longComment: Bowers had a 21-yard touchdown reception in the third quarter and came one yard short of scoring again on a 33-yard catch on a fourth-quarter drive that ended with a Kirk Cousins interception in the end zone. The star TE has reached 70 receiving yards in all seven of his appearances this season and is up to six touchdowns. Bowers came five receiving yards shy of his season high and continues to roll, even as the 4-5 Raiders drop out of contention in the AFC. He'll likely face more resistance in Week 10 against the Seahawks, who just held Cardinals TE Trey McBride to 54 yards.

injury.comment: Williams rushed 20 times for 101 yards and a touchdown and brought in four of five targets for 23 yards in the Cowboys' 27-23 win over the Colts on Sunday.
injury.longComment: Williams turned in one of his more efficient performances against an inconsistent Colts defense, ultimately managing his second 100-yard effort of the season. Williams continued to serve as a prolific supplier of touchdowns as well, recording his ninth rushing score of the campaign on a one-yard run with 1:08 remaining to seal the victory for Dallas. Williams' week-to-week yardage production has fluctuated a fair amount, but his high-volume role and trusted red-zone presence keeps him a must-play despite a tough Week 10 home matchup against the 49ers next Sunday.

injury.comment: Hubbard carried the ball 16 times for 79 yards and caught four of five targets for 17 yards in Sunday's 26-21 loss to Denver.
injury.longComment: The 27-year-old RB nearly produced 100-plus scrimmage yards for the fifth time in the last six games but fell just short. Hubbard remains on track for a career-best campaign, and through eight games he's delivered 619 yards and five TDs on the ground while adding a 26-167-2 line on 31 targets. He lines up for a juicy matchup in Week 10 against the Saints.

injury.comment: Jefferson stands to benefit from Tuesday's acquisition of Kirk Cousins, who is expected to take over as the Vikings' starting quarterback beginning with Sunday's game against the Packers, Michael F. Florio of ESPN.com reports.
injury.longComment: Jefferson averaged a career-low 56.1 receiving yards per game through the first eight contests while the Vikings had the likes of Kyler Murray (hamstring), Carson Wentz and Max Brosmer under center, but the star receiver looks to be one of the biggest winners in the aftermath of the deadline. He'll be reunited with Cousins, who was at the helm for Jefferson's first four years in the league, when the wideout averaged 98.0 yards per contest and had a 17-game pace of 1,671 yards and 8.5 touchdowns. Though Cousins is three years older than when he last donned a Vikings uniform, he enjoyed a resurgent start to the season in Las Vegas, ranking second in the NFL in passing touchdowns (20) and fifth in passing yards (2,340) despite playing behind a weak offensive line and working with an underwhelming receiver group. Cousins' hot start and history with Jefferson should give Jefferson's fantasy managers added confidence in his rest-of-season outlook.

injury.comment: McMillan caught four of six targets for 56 yards and a touchdown in Sunday's 26-21 loss to the Broncos.
injury.longComment: The second-year wideout caught Bryce Young's third TD of the afternoon, a four-yard toss late in the fourth quarter that gave the Panthers some late hope. It was McMillan's first trip to the end zone since Week 4, and through eight games he's collected a 46-625-3 line on 71 targets. He'll look to build on this performance in a Week 10 road trip to New Orleans.

injury.comment: Lawrence completed 16 of 26 passes for 242 yards with a touchdown and no interceptions while rushing once for minus-1 yard in the Jaguars' 33-16 win over the Ravens on Thursday night.
injury.longComment: Lawrence unsurprisingly didn't have a high-volume night, as the Jaguars were progressively able to take control of the game with Joe Fagnano under center for the Ravens. The veteran signal-caller hit Parker Washington on a 50-yard catch-and-run touchdown over the middle just before halftime for his one scoring pass, and Lawrence connected with eight different targets overall on the night. The 2021 first overall pick has now thrown for 1,932 yards with an 18:4 TD:INT and added 79 yards on the ground heading into a Week 10 road matchup against the Titans on Sunday, Nov. 15.

injury.comment: Tuten (ankle/foot) doesn't have an injury designation for Sunday's matchup with Tennessee, Michael DiRocco of ESPN.com reports.
injury.longComment: Tuten played through the injury last week without practicing, and he'll now suit up for Week 10 after just one limited practice Friday. Chris Rodriguez (hand) also is cleared to play and could help ease the burden if Jacksonville is wary of overworking Tuten while he's banged up.

injury.comment: London caught all five of his targets for 68 yards in Sunday's 34-17 loss to the Bengals.
injury.longComment: Cincinnati's secondary did a good job of limiting London's looks from Michael Penix, but the fifth-year wideout still led Atlanta in receiving yards, although Bijan Robinson caught one more pass and Charlie Woerner hauled in the QB's only touchdown. London has gotten only 11 targets over the last two games, turning them into a disappointing 6-76-0 line, and he could have a hard time breaking out in Week 10 against a stingy Kansas City secondary.

injury.comment: Wilson (concussion) reportedly cleared the concussion protocol and is expected to play in Sunday's game versus the Bills, per Ian Rapoport of NFL Network.
injury.longComment: Wilson sat out last Sunday in Kansas City due to a concussion that he sustained one week prior, but he was able to practice fully Friday before being listed as questionable for Week 10, signaling that he was closing in on completing the protocol for head injuries. Following Rapoport's report, that seemingly has come to pass, and his status for Sunday's matchup will be clarified about 90 minutes before a 1:00 p.m. ET kickoff.

tg.callText: [strong] Coach Aaron Glenn said Friday (Nov 13) that Wilson has one step left in the concussion protocol and he expects it done before Sunday; Wilson practiced fully Friday, and Matt Zenitz (CBS, Nov 14) reports he's expected to be cleared. injury.comment: Prescott completed 21 of 34 passes for 335 yards with two touchdowns and no interceptions while rushing twice for one yard in the Cowboys' 27-23 win over the Colts on Sunday. He also lost a fumble.
injury.longComment: Prescott had a couple of bumps in the road against an inconsistent Colts defense, but the veteran signal-caller, who was also working without George Pickens (hamstring), still found his way to his third 300-yard effort of the season. Prescott unsurprisingly bestowed plenty of attention on CeeDee Lamb, who ultimately was responsible for 10 of his completions, 195 of his yards and one of his two TDs. Prescott also connected with Jake Ferguson for a 10-yard scoring strike early in the second quarter, and the one blemish on the star quarterback's day was a  fumble on a sack at his own 16-yard line that led to a Colts touchdown. Prescott has at least one touchdown pass in every game heading into a Week 10 home showdown against the 49ers next Sunday.

injury.comment: The Cardinals placed Wilson (neck) on injured reserve Tuesday.
injury.longComment: Wilson's move to IR was merely a formality, after head coach Mike LaFleur announced Monday that the wideout would be sidelined for the rest of the season after sustaining a fractured vertebra in his neck during Sunday's 17-3 loss to the Seahawks. Per Josh Weinfuss of ESPN.com, Wilson is expected to be in a neck brace for the next six weeks to two months, but the Cardinals don't view the injury as a long-term or career-threatening concern. The 26-year-old receiver will finish the 2026 campaign with 51 receptions for 546 yards and two touchdowns on 88 targets to go with 28 rushing yards on three carries across his nine appearances.

injury.comment: Jacobs underwent surgery on his fractured right ring finger Friday and "should be back in the next few weeks," Tom Pelissero of Netflix reports.
injury.longComment: Jacobs fractured his finger in last week's victory over the Patriots, and he underwent a procedure Friday to repair it. It's unclear exactly how much time he will miss, but he has been ruled out for Week 10 and has avoided injured reserve for the time being, so reports of him missing 2-to-3 weeks appear accurate. It's unclear exactly how things will shake out in Green Bay's backfield while Jacobs works his way back, but all of MarShawn Lloyd, Kaleb Johnson, Chris Brooks (ankle) and Pierre Strong are candidates to fill roles.

injury.longComment: After being listed as limited on five consecutive injury reports going back to last week due to a hamstring issue, Pickens practiced fully Friday and thus is set to miss just one game as a result. In eight appearances so far this season, he's talled a 39-533-2 line on 62 targets.

injury.comment: Washington secured two of seven targets for 61 yards and a touchdown in the Jaguars' 33-10 win over the Ravens on Thursday night. He also returned one punt for 11 yards.
injury.longComment: Washington led the Jaguars in targets while tying for second in receptions and receiving yards on the night. The fourth-year receiver snapped a two-game touchdown drought, crossing the goal line from 50 yards out on a catch and run over the middle with under a minute remaining in the first half. Washington has eclipsed 60 receiving yards in three of the past four games heading into a Week 10 road matchup against the Titans on Sunday, Nov. 15.

injury.comment: Rice secured five of seven targets for 49 yards in the Chiefs' 35-12 win over the Jets on Sunday.
injury.longComment: Rice led the Chiefs in targets while finishing as the runner-up in both receptions and receiving yards. The veteran receiver has been busy the last two games while turning 15 targets into a 12-102-1 line, but he has just one catch of 20-plus yards in that span. Rice is averaging a relatively modest 11.7 yards per catch heading into a Week 10 road matchup against the Falcons.

injury.comment: In addition to the Chiefs team doctors reviewing Mahomes' (throwing) elbow scans, the team sought further feedback from renowned doctors from the Kansas City Royals and Texas Rangers, Adam Schefter of ESPN reports.
injury.longComment: After getting second and third opinions from Dr. Vincent Key (the Royals' head team physician) and Dr. Keith Meister (the Rangers' team physician and orthopedic consultant), it was determined that Mahomes had suffered a muscle strain as well as what a source described as "a very small sprain of his UCL." Per Schefter's report, all of the doctors believed that it was safe for Mahomes play through the issue, despite the fact that the star QB was sore and continued receiving treatment throughout this week. In any case, Mahomes was listed as a full practice participant Wednesday through Friday, and approaches Sunday's game against the Falcons -- which is in line to be the Chiefs debut of trade deadline acquisition WR Josh Downs -- without an injury designation, thus confirming his Week 10 availability.

tg.callText: [strong] He was a full participant in Wednesday's practice (Nov. 11, 2026), and CBS says the elbow problem is "something he'll continue to play through."

injury.comment: Pollard (finger/rest) was a full participant in Friday's practice and doesn't carry an injury designation ahead of Sunday's game against the Jaguars, Jim Wyatt of the Titans' official site reports.
injury.longComment: Pollard sat out Thursday's session with a listed combo of 'finger/rest,' but given that he worked fully Friday, it was likely more of a maintenance day for Tennessee's clear-cut top back. In that role, Pollard has made his mark from a fantasy perspective by averaging 16.6 carries for 74.4 yards, with 14 catches for 70 yards and six rushing scores in eight games to date.

injury.comment: Evans (Achilles) has been ruled out for Sunday's game at Dallas, Nick Wagoner of ESPN reports.
injury.longComment: Evans thus will miss his third game in a row due to the right Achilles injury that he aggravated during a Week 6 win against the Commanders. Head coach Kyle Shanahan said on KNBR radio Thursday that Evans is "real close" to returning to action and likely would play this weekend if it was a playoff matchup. Instead, the 49ers will continue to exercise caution with their No. 1 WR. With Evans again sidelined Sunday, Deebo Samuel (hamstring), Keenan Allen, Demarcus Robinson, Jordan Watkins, Brandin Cooks and Jacob Cowing represent the options at the position available to QB Brock Purdy.

injury.comment: Hall (quadriceps) rushed 15 times for 61 yards and caught three of four targets for 26 yards in Sunday's 35-12 loss to the Chiefs.
injury.longComment: Hall reclaimed the lead role in his first action since Week 3, notching 87 yards on 18 touches compared to 54 yards and a lost fumble on 10 touches for Braelon Allen. The 25-year-old Hall has racked up at least 16 touches in all four of his appearances this season, and the 22-year-old Allen's four consecutive games over 100 scrimmage yards entering Sunday's action weren't enough to pry the starting role away from Hall. Expect Hall to continue leading the backfield in Week 10 against the Bills, with his superior receiving ability likely to come into play if the 2-7 Jets fall behind as expected.

injury.comment: Young completed 28 of 39 passes for 276 yards and three touchdowns with one interception in Sunday's 26-21 loss to the Broncos. He added 13 yards on his only carry and lost a fumble.
injury.longComment: The fourth-year QB tossed TDs in each of the last three quarters, finding Tommy Tremble, Darren Waller and Tetairoa McMillan, but Young's attempt to engineer a game-winning drive inside the final two minutes ended on a Nik Bonitto strip sack. It's the third time this season Young has thrown three touchdowns, but his first such performance since Week 2. He'll take a 16:6 TD:INT through eight games into a Week 10 clash with the Saints.

injury.comment: Moore secured three of five targets for 25 yards and rushed once for 11 yards in the Bills' 23-6 win over the Vikings on Monday night.
injury.longComment: The veteran receiver came into the game without an injury designation related to the shoulder issue he's managing, but Moore still put together a modest performance against a tough Vikings defense that kept pressure on Josh Allen throughout the night. Moore has a combined 7-107-1 line on on 12 targets in the two contests he's suited up for since returning from a two-game absence, and he should have a much better chance of downfield success in a Week 10 road matchup against the Jets' vulnerable defense Sunday.

injury.comment: Marks will be the Texans' lead back against the Browns on Sunday after David Montgomery (groin) was ruled out for that contest.
injury.longComment: Montgomery was initially tagged as questionable for Week 10 after logging a full practice Friday, but the veteran running back will end up missing a fourth straight game due to a groin injury. That means Marks will once again operate as Houston's RB1 while Emari Demercado and Dare Ogunbowale -- the latter of whom was signed to the practice squad and elevated to the active roster Saturday -- provide backfield depth. Marks has logged at least 15 carries in each of his last four outings, and over that span, he has turned 67 carries into 254 yards (3.8 YPC) and added eight catches on 12 targets for 67 yards. He has not found the end zone since Week 4 against the Cowboys.

injury.comment: Coker caught four of five targets for 29 yards in Sunday's 26-21 loss to the Broncos.
injury.longComment: It was yet another quiet game from Coker, who has been held below 40 receiving yards in four of the last five games. Since his massive 8-138-2 receiving line in Week 1, Coker has averaged just 3.8 catches for 65.5 receiving yards per game over his last six contests. He has only one touchdown during that span. Coker will be in a bounce-back spot against the Saints at the Superdome next Sunday.

injury.comment: Charbonnet took 16 carries for 77 yards and tallied one catch (on two targets) for nine yards during Sunday's 17-3 win versus the Cardinals.
injury.longComment: The script in the Seahawks backfield flipped from Week 8 to this Sunday, as Charbonnet nearly doubled his touch count (nine vs. 17) while Jadarian Price maintained it (12 vs. 13). Charbonnet also was far more effective with his workload, going from 29 yards from scrimmage to 86. This marked only his second outing since tearing his left ACL back in January, so he figures to keep improving his efficiency while seemingly taking on a greater share of the RB reps over Price.

injury.comment: Jones rushed five times for 16 yards and brought in his only target for five yards in the Vikings' 23-6 loss to the Bills on Monday night.
injury.longComment: Jones and backfield mate Jordan Mason combined for just 11 carries on an abysmal night for the Vikings offense, and the latter was much more efficient than Jones by averaging 5.8 yards per carry on his six totes. Jones now has seen his rushing yardage totals drop in three straight games, and Mason's return from injured reserve has played a role in the former seeing just 18 total carries in the last three contests. Jones retains a very modest outlook for a Week 10 road matchup against his old Packers teammates Sunday.

injury.comment: Darnold (quadriceps), who won't play this coming Sunday at Las Vegas, is expected to return in Week 12 at San Francisco on Sunday, Nov. 29 after a Week 11 bye, Gregg Bell of Sports Radio 93.3 KJR Seattle reports.
injury.longComment: Darnold is one week removed from suffering a quad injury and cracked ribs in a Week 8 loss to the Bears, which sidelined him Sunday against the Cardinals and will keep him in street clothes in Week 10. For as long as Darnold is sidelined, Drew Lock (oblique) is lined up to be the Seahawks' starting quarterback.

injury.comment: Running backs coach Duce Staley said Saturday that Judkins' lower snap count against the Saints in Week 9 was "situational football," Mary Kay Cabot of The Cleveland Plain Dealer reports.
injury.longComment: Judkins was on the field for a season-low 25 offensive snaps in Week 9, which was considerably lower than Dylan Sampson's 47, although the former led Cleveland's backfield with 15 carries, which he turned into 43 yards (4.3 YPC). Judkins has averaged 2.6 yards per carry over his last two outings, and he faces a Texans defense Sunday that ranks 12th in the NFL in rushing yards allowed per game (103.0).

injury.comment: The Saints activated Etienne (hamstring) from injured reserve Saturday, but he remains questionable for Sunday's game against the Panthers, Nick Underhill of NewOrleans.Football reports.
injury.longComment: Etienne thus is poised for his first game action since Week 3, when he strained his left hamstring. His status will be confirmed about 90 minutes before Sunday's 1:00 p.m. ET kickoff, but assuming he's active, he'll join a backfield currently occupied by Alvin Kamara and Audric Estime.

tg.callText: [strong] The Saints activated him from injured reserve on Saturday, Nov 14, and ESPN's Adam Schefter reported he is expected to play, after he practiced Wednesday through Friday (sources disagree on whether Friday was full or limited).

injury.comment: Samuel (hamstring) doesn't have a designation for Sunday's game in Dallas, Nick Wagoner of ESPN reports.
injury.longComment: Samuel was back on the practice field this week for the first time since injuring his right hamstring in Week 5 at Seattle, turning in limited sessions Wednesday and Thursday. It was enough to get the clear to return to action this weekend. With Mike Evans (Achilles) out again, Samuel likely will be among the top WRs at the disposal of QB Brock Purdy along with newcomer Keenan Allen, Demarcus Robinson and Jordan Watkins.

injury.comment: The Vikings are targeting Week 12 against the Falcons on Sunday, Nov. 29, for a return for Murray (hamstring), Tom Pelissero of Netflix reports.
injury.longComment: Murray suffered a Grade 2 hamstring injury during the Vikings' Week 8 loss to the Lions, which prevented him from playing against the Bills in Week 9. The Vikings acquired Kirk Cousins from the Raiders on Tuesday, and the veteran QB will start under center against the Packers on Sunday, with Carson Wentz serving as the backup and Max Brosmer as the emergency QB3 in Murray's absence. It's unclear whether Murray will be ahead of Wentz on the depth chart once the former is cleared to return.

tg.callText: [strong] His hamstring kept him out of Wednesday's (Nov 11) estimated practice, Rotoworld says the Grade 2 strain means he'll miss multiple games, and he's listed Doubtful.

injury.comment: Jeanty rushed six times for 25 yards while catching five of seven targets for minus-5 yards in Sunday's 38-17 loss to the 49ers.
injury.longComment: The Raiders largely abandoned the run after going down 14-0 early, but Jeanty was more effective with his six carries than Mike Washington, who rushed six times for minus-3 yards and finished without a target. Sunday's even distribution in carries was a positive development for Jeanty, who had just two rushing attempts to Washington's 25 in the Week 8 win over the Jets. Jeanty still has more receiving yards (371) than rushing yards (362) and is averaging just 3.2 yards per carry heading into a difficult Week 10 matchup against Seattle's elite front seven.

injury.comment: Allen rushed eight times for 33 yards, caught both of his targets for 21 yards and lost a fumble in Sunday's 35-12 loss to the Chiefs.
injury.longComment: Allen was limited to 10 touches in Breece Hall's (quadriceps) return from a five-game absence, while Hall turned 18 touches into 87 yards. The 22-year-old Allen excelled during Hall's absence, topping 100 scrimmage yards in each of the previous four games, but Allen will be tough to trust moving forward in fantasy with Hall first in line for touches, especially in the negative game scripts that will likely persist for the 2-7 Jets. Allen's lost fumble was his first of the season, and he has put the ball on the ground only one other time, so at least ball security hasn't been an issue for him heading into a Week 10 home game against the Bills.

injury.comment: Cooper (ankle), who is listed as questionable for Sunday's game against the Bills, is expected to be available, Matt Zenitz of CBS Sports reports.
injury.longComment: Cooper was working through an ankle issue during Week 10 prep and drew the questionable tag after logging a full practice Friday. The rookie first-round wide receiver is on track to suit up Sunday, and the same goes for Garrett Wilson (concussion) and Adonai Mitchell (knee). Wilson did not play against the Chiefs in Week 9, and in his absence, Cooper caught a season-high eight passes (on 11 targets) for 58 yards in a 35-12 loss for the Jets.

tg.callText: [strong] Cooper (ankle) was limited Wednesday and Thursday, practiced fully Friday (Nov 13) and is listed questionable; Matt Zenitz (CBS, Nov 14) reports he's expected to be available.

injury.comment: The Vikings have already gauged Cousins' interest in returning to the team in 2027 since acquiring him Tuesday in a trade with the Raiders, Ian Rapoport of NFL Network reports.
injury.longComment: Cousins -- who will start Sunday's game in Green Bay as he dons a Minnesota uniform for the first time since 2023 -- is set to become a free agent in the spring, but if all goes well over the next several weeks, the Vikings are hoping that the 38-year-old quarterback can be more than just a half-season rental. At the very least, Cousins is expected to provide an upgrade under center from the likes of Kyler Murray (hamstring) and Carson Wentz, both of whom struggled to move the chains while Minnesota raced to a 6-2 start thanks in large part to its blitz-happy, aggressive defense. During his time in Las Vegas, Cousins tossed 20 touchdown passes (second in NFL) and compiled 2,340 passing yards (fifth in NFL), despite playing alongside one of the league's weaker wide-receiver groups.

injury.comment: Mason rushed six times for 35 yards and brought in two of three targets for seven yards in the Vikings' 23-6 loss to the Bills on Monday night.
injury.longComment: Mason was markedly more efficient than backfield mate Aaron Jones with his opportunities, averaging 5.8 yards per carry compared to the latter's 3.2. Both backs' touches were limited due to game script, however, but Mason's YPC was an encouraging figure. The veteran back next takes aim at the Packers defense in a Week 10 road matchup on Sunday.

injury.comment: Shakir secured all four targets for 58 yards in the Bills' 23-6 win over the Vikings on Monday night.
injury.longComment: Shakir tied for the team lead in receptions while setting the pace in receiving yards on a night when Josh Allen spread the ball around to eight different targets. The veteran receiver continues to maintain his trademark steady presence in Buffalo's air attack, now having recorded at least Monday night's catch and yardage tallies in four of the last five games. Shakir carries a bright outlook into a Week 10 road matchup against a vulnerable Jets defense on Sunday.

injury.comment: Flournoy caught two of three targets for 53 yards during Sunday's 27-23 win over the Colts.
injury.longComment: Flournoy had a chance to operate in a more prominent role on offense with George Pickens (hamstring) inactive, but Flournoy ultimately finished with his fewest catches since Week 3, despite playing 77 of 79 offensive snaps. The wide receiver helped set up Dallas for the game-winning score late in the fourth quarter, reeling in a deep ball from quarterback Dak Prescott for a 46-yard gain. Flournoy now has reeled in 32 of 47 targets for 395 yards and two touchdowns over nine contests so far during the 2026 campaign.

injury.comment: The Dolphins hope Willis (abdomen) will return this year but haven't ruled out season-ending surgery, Joe Schad of The Palm Beach Post reports.
injury.longComment: With that in mind, coach Jeff Hafley noted that Willis had an MRI to assess his core muscle injury and will continue to explore medical opinions. The team already placed Willis on injured reserve, ruling him out through Week 13. The latest report suggests that it's still unclear whether Willis will miss four games, the rest of the season or something in between. Kyle McCord is taking over at QB for the Dolphins in the meantime, with Hafley on Wednesday noting of Willis' job security in general, "He'll be the starting quarterback if he returns."

injury.comment: Montgomery (groin) has been downgraded from questionable to out for Sunday's game against the Browns.
injury.longComment: Montgomery drew the questionable tag for Week 10 after logging a full practice Friday. However, the veteran running back has not progressed enough in his recovery from a groin injury to return for Sunday's contest, which will mark his fourth consecutive absence. With Montgomery sidelined, Woody Marks will once again serve as the Texans' RB1 while Emari Demercado provides backfield depth. Montgomery's next chance to play is Week 11 against the Colts on Thursday.

injury.comment: Boston (toe), who is listed as questionable for Sunday's game against the Texans, is expected to play barring a surprise, Jeremy Fowler of ESPN reports.
injury.longComment: After missing practice Wednesday and Thursday, Boston returned to a limited session Friday, with coach Todd Monken noting that the WR was "trending in the right way." Now, assuming no setbacks in warmups, it appears as though Boston will be available versus Houston, with his official game status set to be confirmed once Cleveland's inactives are posted about 90 minutes before Sunday's 1 pm ET kickoff.

injury.comment: Tate (shoulder) has been ruled out for Sunday's game against the Jaguars, Jim Wyatt of the Titans' official site reports.
injury.longComment: There was previously some optimism that Tate -- who last played in Week 7 -- would be able to return after the Titans' Week 9 bye, but the wideout's absence will continue at least until Nov. 22 against the Cowboys, a contest that coach Robert Saleh is hopeful the No. 4 overall pick in the NFL draft will be back for, per Turron Davenport of ESPN.com. For now, added WR snaps/targets will be available for Chimere Dike and Elic Ayomanor alongside Wan'Dale Robinson, with Calvin Ridley also mixing in, an arrangement that was in play during Tennessee's Nov. 1 loss to the Bengals.

injury.comment: The Browns announced Wednesday that Watson (concussion) will start Sunday's game against the Texans, Kelsey Russo of the team's official site reports.
injury.longComment: Watson cleared the NFL's five-step concussion protocol this past Saturday, but because he managed just one limited practice during Week 9 prep, the Browns opted to make him inactive for their matchup with the Saints. Shedeur Sanders drew his first start of the season and threw for 297 yards and two touchdowns in the team's 23-22 overtime loss in New Orleans, but he'll return to the No. 2 role this week while a healthy Watson reclaims the starting job. Though the Browns have gone 5-3 with Watson under center this season, he hasn't been without his flaws (six turnovers, 33 sacks taken). As such, Watson may need a strong showing against the Texans to hold off Sanders for the starting job in the weeks to come.

injury.comment: Price posted nine carries for 24 yards and secured all four targets for 54 yards during Sunday's 17-3 victory versus the Cardinals.
injury.longComment: Price received one more touch than Week 8's 12 but more than doubled his yards from scrimmage from 37 to 78. Having said that, backfield mate Zach Charbonnet went from nine touches last Monday against the Bears to 17 in Week 9 while pacing the Seahawks in total yards with 86. Price and Charbonnet appear poised to split the RB reps moving forward, but the former may be the change-of-pace option while the latter handles early downs.

injury.comment: Rodriguez (hand) doesn't carry an injury designation for Sunday's game against the Titans, Michael DiRocco of ESPN.com reports.
injury.longComment: Rodriguez was listed as a limited practice participant all week,  but his hand issue is something he'll play through, while working alongside Bhayshul Tuten (ankle/foot), who returned to a limited session Friday and was also cleared for Week 10 action. Rodriguez has 55 carries in eight games to date, while Tuten has logged 122 rushes in that span, but Rodriguez has at least helped out his fantasy managers of late by scoring in each of his last two contests.

injury.comment: Allen will play for the 49ers in Sunday's game at Dallas after being acquired in a trade earlier this week, David Lombardi of SFStandard.com reports.
injury.longComment: Allen could have a significant role immediately, joining an injury-riddled WR room, though Deebo Samuel (hamstring) has been cleared to play this Sunday. Mike Evans (Achilles) is out again, leaving Samuel, Allen, Demarcus Robinson and Jordan Watkins as the top healthy options at wide receiver. San Francisco coach Kyle Shanahan mentioned Wednesday that Allen still has some risk of being suspended at some point this season due to an August arrest for DUI while he was with the Colts, per 95.7 The Game.

injury.comment: Tucker caught four of eight targets for 55 yards during Sunday's 38-17 loss to the 49ers.
injury.longComment: Tucker finished tied for the team lead in targets with tight end Brock Bowers, garnering at least five targets for the fifth time in the team's last six contests. The wide receiver rebounded well after being blanked in Week 8 versus the Jets, securing four or more receptions for the seventh time this season. Tucker has now reeled in 33 of 56 targets for 529 yards and four touchdowns over the Raiders' first nine games during the 2026 campaign.

injury.comment: Kincaid (ankle) doesn't have an injury designation for Sunday's game against the Jets.
injury.longComment: Kincaid was a full practice participant Friday after logging limited sessions the previous two days. He should be fine for his usual role against a porous Jets defense.

injury.comment: Lock (right elbow/oblique) doesn't have a designation for Sunday's game at Las Vegas, Brady Henderson of ESPN reports.
injury.longComment: Lock was listed as limited on the Seahawks' first two Week 10 injury reports due to a lingering right elbow issue and a new oblique concern. He spoke of the latter injury Thursday, telling Curtis Crabtree of Fox 13 Seattle that he's "feeling good," and Lock's ability to avoid a designation confirms as much ahead of Sunday's matchup. In three appearances (two starts) this season, Lock has completed 54 of 76 passes (71 percent) for 597 yards, five touchdowns and no interceptions.

injury.comment: Black rushed 11 times for 70 yards but wasn't targeted in Sunday's 38-17 win over the Raiders.
injury.longComment: Black led the 49ers in rushing yards, finishing with two more than Christian McCaffrey, but McCaffrey operated as the clear lead back and scored twice on 20 touches. McCaffrey won't be unseated as the starter while healthy, but Black has started to earn a larger role, with double-digit carries for at least 63 rushing yards in consecutive games. The rookie third-round pick is averaging a solid 4.5 yards per carry heading into a Week 10 road game against the Cowboys.

injury.comment: Sampson rushed eight times for 21 yards while catching three of six targets for 27 yards during Sunday's 23-22 overtime loss against the Saints.
injury.longComment: Sampson toted the rock a season-high eight times, but he averaged a minimal 2.6 yards per carry. The running back remained heavily involved in the passing game, tying wide receiver KC Concepcion for second on the team in targets behind wideout Denzel Boston (seven). Sampson has now reeled in three or more passes in three straight games, and he figures to remain most valuable as a pass catcher for fantasy managers ahead of the team's Week 10 matchup with Houston.

injury.comment: Kamara (rest/back) was a full practice participant Thursday.
injury.longComment: Kamara was listed as a non-participant Wednesday due to the combination of rest and back, but his return to all drills one day later gives him the all-clear ahead of Sunday's contest versus the Panthers. He may be welcoming back fellow RB Travis Etienne (hamstring) in Week 10 after the latter was designated for return from IR and so far has managed a pair of limited sessions, while Audric Estime is coming off a 16-touch showing this past Sunday versus the Browns.

injury.comment: When asked Wednesday whether Pierce (heel) has a chance to return from IR this season, Colts head coach Shane Steichen was noncommittal, James Boyd of The Athletic reports.
injury.longComment: "We'll see. Like I said last week, he's still in that rehab process, and I'm not going to put a timetable on return," Steichen noted of the wideout, who's been on IR since Sept. 26. At 2-7, the Colts were sellers ahead of the NFL's trade deadline, so the team presumably has no reason rush Pierce back. With Keenan Allen and Josh Downs no longer in the mix, Indy's healthy WRs for now are Ashton Dulin, Laquon Treadwell, Anthony Gould, Deion Burks and Nick Westbrook-Ikhine.

injury.comment: Saints coach Kellen Moore said Wednesday that Tyson should get "a healthy dose more" of snaps in Sunday's game against the Panthers, Jeff Nowak of WWL Radio reports.
injury.longComment: Tyson played just 18 snaps and lost a fumble on his first catch this past Sunday against the Browns, but there were some positives from his regular-season debut, including a strong target rate (five targets on 16 routes). While there's no assurance of a full-time role, Tyson at least figures to take more snaps away from fellow rookie Bryce Lance, if not from veteran Devaughn Vele.

injury.comment: Penix completed 20 of 31 passes for 162 yards and a touchdown with an interception in Sunday's 34-17 loss to Cincinnati. He added 50 rushing yards on three carries.
injury.longComment: It looked like it would be a big day for the Falcons offense when Penix led his team to points on its first two drives. including a one-yard TD to Charlie Woerner, but Atlanta managed just seven more points over the final three quarters. The touchdown pass was Penix's 10th of the season, setting a new career high, but he's also been picked off five times in the last two games after throwing only one INT in his first five contests of 2026. He'll face a tough test in Week 10 against Kansas City.

injury.comment: Johnson rushed once for one yard and caught both of his targets for 36 yards against the Vikings in a 23-6 victory Monday.
injury.longComment: Johnson got just one carry while workhorse No. 1 RB James Cook logged a hearty 31 totes. However, Johnson made one big play as a receiver, hauling in a 36-yard reception on a third-down play early in the third quarter to bring Buffalo into Vikings territory. While Johnson has been nearly invisible as a ball carrier this season, he's been effective in a pass-catching role, racking up 210 yards on 17 catches through six games.

injury.comment: Washington turned six carries into minus-three yards in Sunday's 38-17 loss to the 49ers.
injury.longComment: The rookie running back wasn't targeted in the passing game. One week after getting a trial run as the Raiders' clear lead back, a game in which he produced 83 yards on 25 carries, Washington was out-snapped 32 to 17 by Ashton Jeanty against San Francisco. He's averaging just 3.9 yards per carry on 71 totes this season and has just three receptions, though it's worth noting that Jeanty has been even less efficient as a ball carrier with only 3.1 YPC. Washington is a fantasy bench stash, but the Raiders' rushing attack seems broken as a whole.

injury.comment: Mitchell (knee) is listed as questionable for Sunday's game against the Bills but is expected to play, Matt Zenitz of CBS Sports reports.
injury.longComment: Mitchell, Garrett Wilson (concussion) and Omar Cooper (ankle) all practiced in full Friday. Each of them were tagged as questionable, but it appears as though the Jets will be with all three of their top wide receivers for Sunday's AFC East tilt. Mitchell failed to haul in any of his seven targets in Week 9 against the Chiefs, but he did record seven catches (on nine targets) for 142 yards and a touchdown during the Jets' Week 8 loss to the Raiders.

injury.comment: Vele caught two passes for 17 yards on four targets in Sunday's 23-22 overtime win over the Browns.
injury.longComment: With Jordyn Tyson (hamstring) making his regular-season debut against Cleveland, Vele's role remained steady, running 44 routes on Tyler Slough's 46 dropbacks. Bryce Lance and Noah Fant appeared to be the bigger losers in terms of playing time and routes. Still, Tyson figures to have an effect on Vele's target potential moving forward, as he's setting in as more of a low-floor WR4/5 in fantasy.

injury.comment: Fannin (groin) was a full participant in Friday's practice and doesn't have an injury designation for Sunday's game against the Texans, Chris Easterling of the Akron Beacon Journal reports.
injury.longComment: After logging limited sessions Wednesday and Thursday, Fannin's full practice to close the week paves the way for him to continue to lead the Browns' TE corps this weekend. Through nine games thus far, Fannin has yielded fantasy lineup utility by compiling a 37/453/4 receiving line on 53 targets in that span.

injury.comment: Smith completed 18 of 32 passes for 165 yards, no touchdowns and no interceptions in Sunday's 35-12 loss to the Chiefs. He also rushed once for eight yards.
injury.longComment: Smith struggled in the absence of top wide receiver Garrett Wilson (concussion), as the Jets made four field goals in the first half before getting blanked in the second half. The veteran QB posted his second-lowest total of the season for passing yards and was held without a touchdown for the first time since Week 1. Smith could be busy in Week 10 with the 2-7 Jets likely to be forced into a pass-heavy game plan if they fall behind against the Bills.

injury.comment: Lloyd (knee) is not listed on the Packers' injury report Wednesday.
injury.longComment: The running back appears ready to return to the lineup for Sunday's game against the Vikings after missing Week 9 against New England. With Josh Jacobs (finger) set to miss some time, Lloyd figures to be part of the backfield mix, joining Kaleb Johnson and Pierre Strong.

injury.comment: Giddens was active but didn't play in Sunday's 27-23 loss to the Cowboys.
injury.longComment: Giddens didn't see any action after turning six carries into 43 yards in Week 8 against the Jaguars. With Jonathan Taylor potentially set to be traded before Tuesday's NFL trade deadline, Giddens would stand to operate as the team's No. 2 option in the backfield behind rookie Seth McGowan if Taylor departs.

injury.comment: Concepcion caught four of six targets for 85 yards and a touchdown in Sunday's 23-22 overtime loss to the Saints. He added three yards on his only carry.
injury.longComment: Most of Concepcion's production came on a 64-yard TD in the fourth quarter as Shedeur Sanders found him just inside New Orleans' 30-yard line and the speedy rookie -- who briefly exited the contest after sustained what appeared to be a right leg issue -- to did the rest by eluding a couple defenders. It was Concepcion's first career NFL touchdown, and he sports a 37-437-1 line on 55 targets through his first nine games for the Browns. If Sanders takes over from Deshaun Watson (concussion) on a permanent basis, it could lead to plenty more big plays for Concepcion.

injury.comment: Addison (thumb), who listed is questionable for Sunday's contest at Green Bay, is in line to be a game-time decision, Ian Rapoport of NFL Network reports.
injury.longComment: The Vikings will post their list of Week 10 inactives about 90 minutes before Sunday's 1:00 p.m. ET kickoff, so his status seemingly will come down to a pregame workout. He injured his thumb in practice Friday and thus was tagged as questionable ahead of the weekend. With Jauan Jennings (calf) already ruled out, Minnesota's remaining healthy wide receivers not named Justin Jefferson are Myles Price, Tai Felton and Jeshaun Jones.

injury.comment: Minshew suffered a torn UCL in his right throwing elbow last Sunday at Seattle and is slated to undergo season-ending surgery, Adam Schefter of ESPN reports.
injury.longComment: Minshew incredibly played through the injury in Week 9, logging all 53 offensive snaps and completing 21 of 30 passes for 166 yards, no touchdowns and no interceptions in his first start replacing the since-departed Jacoby Brissett. Schefter added that Minshew still is determining the timing of the procedure, but he plans on having it. With Minshew out for the rest of the campaign, rookie third-round pick Carson Beck is taking over under center for the Cardinals.

injury.comment: Johnson will be the Chiefs' top running back for Week 10 after Kenneth Walker (groin) was ruled out for Sunday's game against the Falcons, Adam Schefter of ESPN reports.
injury.longComment: Walker popped up on Friday's practice report as a DNP due to groin tightness, and the injury is severe enough for the fifth-year running back to miss his first game of the season. That leaves Johnson -- the Chiefs' fifth-round pick of the 2026 NFL Draft -- as the lead back for Sunday's game, and with Jaydn Ott (hamstring) listed as questionable, the team could elevate Nate Carter from the practice squad to provide additional backfield depth. Through eight regular-season games, Johnson has turned 26 carries into 111 yards (4.3 YPC) and a touchdown and caught 14 passes on 16 targets for 237 yards and a score.

injury.comment: Knight (concussion) is cleared to play Sunday against the Rams, Josh Weinfuss of ESPN.com reports.
injury.longComment: Knight figures to split backfield work with Tyler Allgeier, who played 96 percent of snaps last week when Knight was inactive for a 17-3 loss at Seattle. Knight suffered the concussion in Week 8, shortly after Jeremiyah Love injured his ankle -- an issue that sent the rookie to injured reserve not long after. Love is out for at least three more games, leaving Allgeier and Knight to split backfield work again.

injury.comment: Brooks (groin) has been downgraded from doubtful to out for Sunday's game against the Saints, Joe Person of The Athletic reports.
injury.longComment: Brooks ended Week 10 prep with back-to-back limited practices, but he was tagged as doubtful for Sunday's game against the Panthers. The third-year running back is not quite fully recovered from a groin injury that landed him on IR in late September, so his next chance to suit up is Week 11 against the Ravens on Sunday, Nov. 22. Trevor Etienne, AJ Dillon and Anthony Tyus will continue to operate in rotational backfield roles behind Chuba Hubbard while Brooks is sidelined.

injury.comment: Chiefs coach Andy Reid said Friday that Downs looks ready to play in Sunday's game at Atlanta, Charles Goldman of AtoZ Sports reports.
injury.longComment: The Chiefs traded for Downs on Tuesday before the deadline and had him on the practice field by Wednesday. Reid stopped short of saying Downs will play, but it sounds like the wideout will have some kind of role this Sunday alongside Rashee Rice and Xavier Worthy.

injury.comment: Washington caught two of three targets for 21 yards during Sunday's 19-9 loss to the Lions.
injury.longComment: Washington was held in check by Detroit's suspect secondary, failing to reel in at least three passes for the first time this season. In addition, his 21 receiving yards were also a season low. The wide receiver has yet to exceed 70 receiving yards in a game this year, and he has reached the end zone only once. Washington will have an opportunity to get back on track against the sputtering Colts in Week 10.

injury.comment: Kelce brought in four of six targets for 72 yards in the Chiefs' 35-12 win over the Jets on Sunday. He also rushed once for one yard.
injury.longComment: Kelce led the Chiefs in receiving yards and finished second in targets on the afternoon, and his tally in the former category also served as the legendary tight end's second highest of the season. Kelce got there with a big boost from a game-high 38-yard catch, and he'll take a formidable 33-482-2 line into a Week 10 road matchup against the Falcons next Sunday.

injury.comment: Sanders will return to a backup role for Sunday's game against the Texans after the Browns announced Wednesday that Deshaun Watson (concussion) will draw the Week 10 start, Kelsey Russo of the team's official site reports.
injury.longComment: Watson led the Browns to a 5-3 record over their first eight games before developing concussion symptoms and being placed in the NFL's five-step protocol last week. Though Watson cleared protocol last Saturday, his lack of on-field reps during the week prompted the Browns to keep him inactive for Sunday's matchup with the Saints. Sanders stepped in under center and overcame a slow start to finish with 297 passing yards, 28 rushing yards, two passing touchdowns and no turnovers in a 23-22 overtime loss, with his performance drawing praise from head coach Todd Monken. Though the Browns will go back to a healthy Watson for Week 10, Sanders' strong outing in New Orleans could put Watson on shakier ground atop the depth chart.

injury.comment: Mendoza will take over as the Raiders' new starting quarterback beginning with Sunday's game versus the Seahawks after Las Vegas traded Kirk Cousins to Minnesota on Tuesday, Adam Schefter of ESPN reports.
injury.longComment: The No. 1 overall pick in the 2026 NFL Draft has opened his professional career on the bench, with his lone action to date coming during garbage time of a blowout loss to the Patriots in Week 5, when he completed six of eight pass attempts for 48 yards. However, with the 4-5 Raiders shipping out Cousins for a 2027 third-round pick, the 23-year-old Mendoza will now be thrust into his first extended NFL playing time and will face a pair of tough defenses off the bat, as he'll follow up the matchup against the Seahawks with a road game in Denver in Week 11. Mendoza had underwhelming numbers over his three preseason appearances, but he's reportedly been "tearing it up in practice" during the regular season and has given the Raiders optimism that he's ready to lead the offense, per Matt Zenitz of CBSSports.com.

injury.comment: Spears (knee) is expected to play Sunday against the Jaguars, Jeremy Fowler of ESPN.com reports.
injury.longComment: Spears, who hasn't played since Week 6, advanced from a 'DNP' on Wednesday to a limited session Thursday, before working fully Friday and being listed as questionable heading into the weekend. His looming return would provide a boost the Titans' Week 10 RB depth, but prior to his injury, Spears' fantasy impact was modest, with 18 carries for 66 yards and 15 catches for 75 yards on 17 targets in six contests.

injury.comment: Johnson could serve as the Packers' lead option on the ground in Sunday's game against the Vikings with Josh Jacobs (finger) expected to miss multiple weeks and with the status of MarShawn Lloyd (knee) uncertain, Matt Schneidman of The Athletic reports.
injury.longComment: After being a healthy inactive for the Packers' previous two games, Johnson suited up for Sunday's tilt with the Patriots while Lloyd was inactive. With Jacobs leaving the contest late in the first quarter after fracturing his right ring finger, Johnson was thrust into action and delivered the Packers' best rushing performance of the season, finishing with 14 carries for 68 yards and a touchdown in the 45-27 win. Head coach Matt LaFleur relayed Monday that Jacobs will need surgery and could land on injured reserve, and while Lloyd could have a chance at returning to action Week 10, the Packers likely came away encouraged enough by Johnson's showing in Foxborough to give him another turn as their lead option on the ground. Johnson isn't likely to earn much passing-down work, however, as Lloyd, Pierre Strong and Chris Brooks (ankle) -- who could return from IR this week -- are all more capable options in that phase.

injury.comment: Coleman finished Monday's 23-6 win over the Vikings with three catches for 17 yards on six targets.
injury.longComment: Going up against a tough Minnesota defense, Bills QB Josh Allen posted a modest 234 passing yards with one touchdown and one interception. He spread the ball around to eight different pass catchers, with none of them hauling in more than four receptions. Coleman actually led Buffalo with six targets, but he finished seventh with just 17 receiving yards. The third-year wideout has been very up-and-down this season, registering 59 or more receiving yards three times but logging 17 or fewer receiving yards on four occasions. That makes his output quite difficult to predict for fantasy purposes.

injury.comment: Fields carried twice for minus-one yard and lost a fumble while logging five snaps on offense in Sunday's 35-12 win over the Jets.
injury.longComment: The Chiefs' backup quarterback saw the field for just the second time this season, after he had previously played one snap in a Week 1 win over the Broncos. Due to head coach Andy Reid's reluctance to use starter Patrick Mahomes on quarterback sneaks, Fields subbed into the game for a third-and-1 play in the first quarter. Fields ended up coughing the football, with the Jets making the recovery. The Chiefs went on to build enough of a lead to rest Mahomes for the final possession of the game with just over two minutes left in the fourth quarter, when Fields proceeded to hand the ball off three times before kneeling to run out the clock.

injury.comment: The Cowboys placed Goodson (knee) on injured reserve Saturday, Tommy Yarrish of the team's official site reports.
injury.longComment: The move comes as no surprise, seeing as Goodson is expected to miss multiple games due to ACL and MCL sprains in his knee that he suffered during the Cowboys' Week 9 victory over the Colts. With Malik Davis (hip, IR) out for the year and Goodson now on IR, Israel Abanikanda -- who was elevated from the practice squad to the active roster Saturday -- will serve as Dallas' RB2 behind Javonte Williams for Sunday's game against the 49ers. Goodson is required to miss at least four games while on IR, so his next chance to play is Week 15 against the Rams on Sunday, Dec. 20.

injury.comment: Robinson caught three passes for 22 yards on four targets in Sunday's 38-17 win over the Raiders.
injury.longComment: Playing in his first game since Week 2 due to a high ankle sprain, Robinson played 51 percent of the Niners' offensive snaps against Las Vegas. San Francisco's wideout situation is a week-to-week thing moving forward, with the Tuesday addition of Keenan Allen and Deebo Samuel (hamstring), Mike Evans (Achilles) and rookie De'Zhaun Stribling (ankle) all likely to return at some point in the near future. Robinson isn't someone to roster in 12-team fantasy leagues.

injury.comment: Davis logged two carries for two yards and didn't catch his only target Monday in a 23-6 victory against the Vikings.
injury.longComment: Davis continues to be sparsely utilized on offense -- he has two or fewer touches in six of eight contests so far this season. He's pretty solidly stuck in Buffalo's No. 3 RB role, behind James Cook (who logged a Herculean 31 totes Monday) and Ty Johnson (who notched just three touches). That will make Davis a poor fantasy play in Week 10 despite going up against a Jets defense that has struggled against the run this season.

injury.comment: Foot
Warren may see more targets after the Colts traded wideouts Josh Downs and Keenan Allen on Tuesday, Chris Bumbaca of ColtsWire reports.
injury.longComment: The trade deadline went as well as possible for Warren's fantasy value, considering the Colts moved their top wide receivers but avoided an all-out purge. The only problem is that Warren is already averaging 7.6 targets per game (fourth among TEs) and producing just 39.3 receiving yards per game and 7.2 yards per catch. Efficiency has been the issue, not volume, and the Colts will likely lean on their running game after declining to trade RB Jonathan Taylor. Improved play from Warren and QB Daniel Jones would probably matter more than another increase in target share.

injury.comment: Allen caught a 46-yard pass in Sunday's 19-9 loss to the Lions. He rushed one time for minus-1 yard.
injury.longComment: Allen's catch came on a fake punt, so it was an outlier of a play. He played just six offensive snaps behind clear RB1 Ollie Gordon. Since joining Miami via waivers last month, Allen has logged 31 snaps on special teams and six on offense. He has no fantasy appeal.

injury.comment: Strong rushed eight times for 22 yards in Sunday's 45-27 win over the Patriots. He added two catches for 11 yards on two targets.
injury.longComment: With Josh Jacobs (finger) knocked out of the game in the first quarter and set to miss several weeks, Strong figures to see his role expand in Green Bay's backfield, though MarShawn Lloyd, Kaleb Johnson and even Chris Brooks (ankle) are likely to also see snaps in the coming weeks. Strong is not a recommended fantasy target in 12-team leagues.

injury.comment: Worthy (hamstring) was a full participant in Wednesday's practice for Kansas City.
injury.longComment: Worthy was considered day-to-day after exiting Sunday's 35-12 win over the Jets in the fourth quarter. A quick return to full practice participation suggests Worthy will be fine for the upcoming matchup with Atlanta on Sunday, but his target share may decline in the second half of the season after Kansas City traded for WR Josh Downs.

injury.comment: Hockenson (wrist) has been ruled out for Sunday's game at Green Bay.
injury.longComment: Hockenson wasn't able to practice in any capacity during Week 10 prep due to wrist and chest injuries and thus will miss his first contest of the campaign. In Hockenson's absence, Ben Yurosek and Gavin Bartholomew will step into more prominent roles in the Vikings offense, while Devin Culp will be a candidate to be elevated from the practice squad.

injury.comment: Head coach Mike LaFleur said Wednesday that Beck will start Sunday's game against the Rams, Darren Urban of the Cardinals' official site reports.
injury.longComment: Arizona first dealt Jacoby Brissett to Baltimore last Friday, and then Gardner Minshew suffered a torn UCL in his right elbow during this past Sunday's game at Seattle and will undergo season-ending surgery. That series of events precedes Beck taking over as the Cards' No. 1 signal-caller, and with eight other skill-position players on reserve lists at the moment, the top talents available to the offense will be TE Trey McBride and RB Tyler Allgeier.

injury.comment: Demercado rushed six times for 16 yards and caught one of two targets for eight yards during Sunday's 44-22 win over the Chargers.
injury.longComment: Demercado was claimed off waivers by the Texans on Oct. 28, and he made his team debut in Week 9 after the team had a Week 8 bye. The running back finished second on the team in carries behind Woody Marks (18), and Demercado could operate as the team's No. 2 option in the backfield again in Week 10 versus Cleveland if David Montgomery (groin) remains sidelined.

injury.comment: Herbert carried the ball once for seven yards and caught two of his three targets for two yards during Atlanta's loss to the Bengals on Sunday.
injury.longComment: Herbert continued to serve a limited role in his first game since being signed to the active roster from the practice squad, as he played just 11 snaps on offense and nine on special teams. With Brian Robinson (hamstring) set to miss at least another three games, Herbert will likely continue to serve as the team's backup running back behind Bijan Robinson.

injury.comment: Myers (ankle) doesn't have an injury designation for Sunday's matchup with Tennessee, Michael DiRocco of ESPN.com reports.
injury.longComment: Meyers has fought through one injury or another for most of the season. This week, he managed limited practices Thursday and Friday, setting him up to play against the last-place Titans.

injury.comment: Harrison (hamstring) is ruled out for Sunday's game against the Browns.
injury.longComment: Harrison's absence leaves more snaps for some combination of Xavier Hutchinson, Kayshon Boutte and Tank Dell, all of whom were productive last week in a win over the Chargers. C.J. Stroud has been spreading the ball around and putting up big numbers in the process, with even Nico Collins seeing his target share suffer as a result. Harrison is unlikely to handle a full-time role even when he gets back to full strength.

injury.comment: Higbee (illness) and Colby Parkinson (rib) have both been cleared to play in Sunday's game against the Cardinals, while fellow tight end Davis Allen (oblique) is listed as questionable, Sarah Barshop of ESPN.com reports.
injury.longComment: With wideout Puka Nacua (knee) placed on injured reserve this week, there's renewed fantasy interest in the Rams' tight ends. Higbee has run a lot of routes without providing production in recent games, but both he and Parkinson could see more targets over the next few weeks, including Sunday in a favorable matchup with Arizona's subpar pass defense.

injury.comment: Wilson didn't log any snaps during Sunday's win over the Cardinals.
injury.longComment: Wilson averaged 18.2 carries for 66.7 yards over six games between Week 2 and Week 7, culminating with a 24-100-1 rushing line against Kansas City. However, that opportunity came while Jadarian Price and Zach Charbonnet were on IR. Both running backs returned ahead of the Week 8 matchup against Chicago, and Wilson hasn't played a single offensive snap in two games since. As long as Charbonnet and Price are both healthy, it appears Wilson is going to be relegated primarily to a special-teams role, if he plays at all.

injury.comment: Wright (quadriceps) was a full participant in Wednesday's practice, C. Isaiah Smalls II of the Miami Herald reports.
injury.longComment: After missing last Sunday's loss to the Lions, Wright figures to be back in as the lightly used RB2 behind Ollie Gordon, though Wright has not produced when on the field this season. He's averaged 1.9 yards per carry on 22 attempts and is virtually a zero in the passing game.

injury.comment: Shaheed (knee) was a full participant in Wednesday's practice, John Boyle of the Seahawks' official site reports.
injury.longComment: Shaheed suffered a knee injury during a Week 7 win against the Chiefs and missed the last two games as a result. Now that he's unhindered on the practice field, though, he'll resume his standing as Seattle's No. 2 WR and primary kick and punt returner

injury.comment: Strange caught both of his targets for 22 yards in Thursday night's 33-10 win over the Ravens.
injury.longComment: The Jaguars keep blowing teams out and aren't being pushed on offense, which is keeping Trevor Lawrence's pass volume low. Strange is still making the most of his few opportunities, totaling four grabs for 77 yards on four targets over the last two weeks, games in which the Jaguars have combined to outscore their opponents 75-17. Strange is a TE1 for fantasy and gets a date with the Titans on Sunday, Nov. 15.

injury.comment: The Bills elevated Buechele from the practice squad to the active roster Saturday.
injury.longComment: It's the first time this season that Buechele has been elevated from the practice squad. He'll likely operate as the Bills' emergency third quarterback behind Josh Allen and Kyle Allen for Sunday's game against the Jets.

injury.comment: Mills completed one of two pass attempts for seven yards and lost two yards on two carries in Sunday's 44-22 win over the Chargers.
injury.longComment: Since the Texans had built their lead to 19 with less than five minutes remaining in the fourth quarter, head coach DeMeco Ryans opted to pull starting quarterback C.J. Stroud from the game and handed the offense over to Mills. In what marked his first playing time of the season, Mills directed two possessions. He led the Texans to a field goal with 2:20 remaining, then knelt twice to run out the clock when Houston got the ball back with 1:07 left. With Stroud enjoying a bounce-back campaign, Mills' opportunities will likely be limited to garbage-time situations if Stroud stays healthy.

injury.comment: Knee - ACL
O'Connell moves to QB No. 2 on the depth chart behind Fernando Mendoza, Sam Warren of The Athletic reports.
injury.longComment: O'Connell is set to back up rookie Mendoza, who replaced recently traded Kirk Cousins as the starting quarterback. O'Connell has been with Las Vegas since the team drafted him in the fourth round of the 2023 NFL Draft. The 28-year-old last appeared in a regular-season game in 2025, completing 10 of 22 attempts for 102 yards.

injury.comment: Undisclosed

McCord will step in as the Dolphins' starting quarterback beginning with Sunday's game at Indianapolis after Miami placed Malik Willis (core) on injured reserve Tuesday, Cameron Wolfe of NFL Network reports.
injury.longComment: A 2025 sixth-round pick of the Eagles, McCord will be making his NFL debut Sunday, after he had been active for each of the 1-7 Dolphins' first eight games but didn't see any playing time behind Willis. Before landing with the Dolphins in a trade prior to Week 1, the 24-year-old signal-caller looked sharp during preseason action as a member of the Packers, completing 46 of 70 passes for 446 yards and a 4:0 TD:INT while adding 16 yards on five carries over three games. Expectations should still be held in check for McCord in his first regular-season action, especially while he'll be working with one of the NFL's weaker collections of skill-position players. The Dolphins are optimistic that Willis will be able to return from IR before the end of the season, but McCord should be primed for at least a four-game run as the team's starter while Willis is sidelined.

injury.comment: The Dolphins elevated Cook from the practice squad to the active roster Saturday.
injury.longComment: The Dolphins placed Malik Willis (abdomen) on injured reserve Tuesday, so Cook will operate as the team's backup quarterback behind Kyle McCord for Sunday's game against the Colts. Cook appeared in five regular-season games (four starts) for the Jets in 2025, when he completed 57.5 percent of his passes for 739 yards, two touchdowns and seven interceptions while rushing for 49 yards on 13 carries.

injury.comment: Brosmer completed six of seven attempts for 58 yards in Monday night's 23-6 loss to the Bills.
injury.longComment: Brosmer replaced Carson Wentz in the fourth quarter of Monday night's game after the offense failed to produce a touchdown drive. Week 9 was Brosmer's first appearance in a 2026 regular-season game. He will likely play a similar backup role behind newly acquired Kirk Cousins as the season progresses, at least until Kyler Murray returns from a hamstring injury.

injury.comment: The 49ers fielded trade inquiries for Jones from the Vikings leading up to Tuesday's deadline, but the quarterback is expected to remain in San Francisco, Dianna Russini of BetUS TV reports.
injury.longComment: Even though starting quarterback Brock Purdy has been a leading MVP candidate through the halfway point of the season, the 49ers still place a premium value on Jones as an insurance option in the event Purdy misses time due to injury. As such, the 49ers' asking price for Jones was too rich for the Vikings, who have since pivoted their focus to acquiring Kirk Cousins from the Raiders.

injury.comment: Milroe will get added reps at practice ahead of Sunday's matchup with the Cardinals, Gregg Bell of Sports Radio 93.3 KJR Seattle reports.
injury.longComment: Milroe is expected to serve as the top backup behind Drew Lock at quarterback in Week 9 with Sam Darnold (quadriceps) sidelined. Milroe has yet to appear in a regular-season contest this season and likely won't do so Sunday unless Lock is forced out of the contest with an injury.

injury.comment: The Cardinals signed Aguilar off the Jaguars' practice squad Tuesday, Jeremy Fowler of ESPN.com reports.
injury.longComment: Arizona has yet to announce a corresponding move, but top quarterback Gardner Minshew could be headed to injured reserve after sustaining a torn ACL in Sunday's loss to the Seahawks that may require season-ending surgery. An undrafted rookie out of Tennessee, Aguilar joins fellow rookie Carson Beck and veteran journeyman Josh Johnson as the healthy options in the Cardinals' quarterback room. Aguilar will likely settle in as the No. 3 option on the depth chart if Minshew is indeed placed on IR.

injury.comment: Robinson (hamstring) was placed on injured reserve Saturday, Marc Raimondi of ESPN.com reports.
injury.longComment: Robinson already has missed two games due to a lingering hamstring injury and now must miss at least the next four outings, meaning his next chance for game action is Sunday, Dec. 13 at Cleveland. In a corresponding move, the Falcons are signing Khalil Herbert from the practice squad to the active roster to continue serving as the No. 2 RB behind workhorse Bijan Robinson.

injury.comment: Undisclosed
The Texans signed Ogunbowale to the practice squad before elevating him to the active roster Saturday.
injury.longComment: Ogunbowale was released by the Texans on Thursday after appearing in each of the team's five prior games. He's opted to stay in Houston as a member of the practice squad, and his elevation to the active roster comes after David Montgomery (groin) was ruled out for Sunday's game against the Browns. Ogunbowale and Emari Demercado will provide backfield depth for the Texans behind RB1 Woody Marks for Week 10.

injury.longComment: Burton was already ruled out for Sunday's game against the Texans due to a calf injury that he picked up against the Saints in Week 9. The injury is severe enough for him to warrant an extended absence, and since he's now on IR, Burton will be required to miss at least four games, so the earliest he can return is Week 15 against the Giants on Sunday, Dec. 20. Since the Browns do not have another fullback on the 53-man roster, the team will likely turn to tight ends Carsen Ryan, Zaire Mitchell-Paden and Blake Whiteheart to provide blocking out of the backfield, per Daniel Oyefusi of ESPN.com.

Abanikanda last saw regular-season action in 2023, when he logged 22 carries for 70 yards (3.2 YPC) and added seven catches on 11 targets for 43 yards across six regular-season games with the Jets.

injury.comment: Green Bay activated Brooks (ankle) from injured reserve Saturday, though he is still questionable for Sunday's Week 10 clash against the Vikings.
injury.longComment: Brooks has missed the required four contests after being placed on injured reserve Oct. 10. He was limited in all three practices this week, and it remains to be seen if he'll suit up Sunday. If Brooks does play, he'll help make up for the backfield absence of Josh Jacobs, who has been ruled out due to a finger injury. MarShawn Lloyd, Kaleb Johnson and Pierre Strong are the Packers' current healthy RBs.

Nate Carter is the only running back on Kansas City's practice squad and would be a top candidate for elevation to the active roster depending on the statuses of both Ott and Walker.

If he sees action, it will be Carter's first appearance of the regular season, and he'll face the team that he suited up for in 2025, when he logged nine carries for 60 yards across seven regular-season contests.

The veteran running back went without a carry for the fourth time over Minnesota's past five games, indicating his lack of a role in the running game. Overall this season, Dallas has been a very small part of the Vikings' offense, recording four carries for 14 yards and five catches for 36 yards (on five targets) through eight contests.

Donaldson (shoulder) has been ruled out for Sunday's game against the Panthers, Nick Underhill of NewOrleans.Football reports.
injury.longComment: Donaldson will miss a third straight game, while Travis Etienne (hamstring) has a chance to return from injured reserve. With Etienne listed as questionable, Audric Estime and Alvin Kamara could have significant roles. Donaldson mostly has played in obvious passing situations this year, often staying in as a blocker.

Davis didn't play any offensive snaps in Sunday's 35-12 loss to the Chiefs.

Davis has rushed 15 times for 44 yards, while recording five grabs for 68 yards on six targets across nine appearances this season.

injury.comment: Hull failed to haul in his lone target during the Cardinals' 17-3 loss to the Seahawks on Sunday.
injury.longComment: Ten of Hull's 12 snaps came on special teams, and he wasn't bale to connect with Gardner Minshew on the latter's pass attempt early in the third quarter. Hull has yet to log a carry through three regular-season appearances with the Cardinals. However, he could operate as the team's RB2 behind Tyler Allgeier for Week 10 against the Rams if Bam Knight doesn't clear the league's concussion protocol for that contest.

injury.longComment: As has been the case all season, James filled a minor role in San Francisco's backfield behind Christian McCaffrey and Kaelon Black. James' three touches Sunday were his second most this season behind the four touches he logged in Week 2 versus Miami. James likely will be relegated to making most of his impact as a returner unless either McCaffrey or Black misses time.

Holani didn't log any touches or targets Sunday in a 17-3 win over Arizona.
injury.longComment: Holani logged just two offensive snaps, by far his lowest count in a game of the season. He's trending toward playing primarily on special teams now that Zach Charbonnet and Jadarian Price are back in the fold at running back for Seattle. Emanuel Wilson also is on the roster, but he didn't see any action at all in Week 10.
